comments.note: MainContentViewModel._activeEditor field tracks the open editor so Dispose() can unsubscribe its CloseRequested event. This resolves the known debt noted in the prior api-surface.md ('no guard against concurrent editor opens') for the dispose path; the concurrent-open scenario itself is still not prevented (two rapid OpenEditorForSelectedMovieCommand calls could create two editor instances), but dispose safety is now correct.

FakeMovieCatalogRepository is constructed but its GetMovieListCallCount is never observed in the rewritten CloseRequested_FromEditor_TriggersMoviesListReload test — the test now only verifies CurrentChildViewModel returned to MoviesListVm. A more precise test would wire a catalog that the sut's MoviesListVm actually uses and count LoadAsync calls. Low priority since the behaviour is covered by the other reload tests.

The two Dispose unsubscription tests (Dispose_UnsubscribesFromNavigationChanged, Dispose_UnsubscribesFromActiveDestinationChanged) verify the absence of an update rather than asserting a hard invariant (e.g. event subscription count). This is acceptable for the current architecture but could be tightened with a FakeNavigationService that exposes a subscription count if the pattern needs to be hardened in a future WP.

summary: All 5 acceptance criteria verified by code inspection and test execution. Build: 0 errors, 0 warnings (TreatWarningsAsErrors confirmed). Tests: 676 passed, 0 failed, 6 skipped (infrastructure integration tests requiring live DB/ffprobe — expected). No regressions detected. Edge cases analysed: null-sender path in OnEditorCloseRequested is safe (nav guard fires correctly); Dispose-while-editor-open is safe (CloseRequested unsubscribed, no crash). comments.note: The OnEditorCloseRequested guard uses 'is not MovieEditorViewModel' + return (early-exit pattern) rather than a positive 'if (is MovieEditorViewModel)' guard — functionally identical, but the inverted style is worth noting for code-review consistency checks.

Dispose_UnsubscribesFromNavigationChanged test currently lacks an explicit assertion — it verifies the handler is detached only implicitly by the fact that CurrentChildViewModel does not update. A future hardening opportunity is to expose a subscription count on FakeNavigationService (already flagged by Developer).

summary: Code review complete — PASS with one Fix-Forward applied. No blocking issues found. MainContentViewModel rewrite is well-structured: clean dual-constructor pattern, correct event subscription and disposal, proper navigation guard in OnEditorCloseRequested, and all five acceptance criteria confirmed met by code inspection. Fix-Forward applied: added missing assertion to Dispose_UnsubscribesFromNavigationChanged (test had no assertion despite documenting intent). 676/676 tests pass post-fix.

comments.note: Dispose_UnsubscribesFromNavigationChanged (MainContentViewModelTests.cs) had no assertion — the test body documented the intent ('CurrentChildViewModel was last set to MoviesListVm') but never called .Should(). Added: b.Sut.CurrentChildViewModel.Should().BeSameAs(b.Sut.MoviesListVm, because: 'after dispose the NavigationChanged handler must be detached'). The test now actually verifies what it claims. 676/676 pass post-fix — confirming the dispose unsubscription was already correct.

OnRefreshStateChanged fires MoviesListVm.LoadAsync(CancellationToken.None) with no error continuation, while OnEditorCloseRequested has an identical LoadAsync call wrapped in .ContinueWith(...OnlyOnFaulted) for error logging. The inconsistency is minor but could silently swallow a load failure after a scan completes. Consider aligning both call sites in a future pass.

MainContentView.axaml.cs OnUnloaded unsubscribes _primaryNavService.ActiveDestinationChanged but does not unsubscribe NavView.SelectionChanged. NavView is co-owned by the same UserControl so GC pressure is minimal, but the asymmetry is a code smell. Low risk; no action required for this WP.

[documentation-forward] StubViewModel is used for the 'filters' and 'settings' primary destinations — it acts as a placeholder until real ViewModels exist. The project manifest's api-surface.md and constraints.md should note that StubViewModel is a temporary placeholder and that destinations consuming it will need real ViewModel implementations before those features are built out.
